pass_a_gloss: [...] of gentleness he makes the showing, saving unexpectedly those who have slipped from every hope, and holding out a saving hand to those somewhere on the ground, and as lying on earth. Something such they say who bring up the prayer set before us. For from the foundation of the world we neither heard nor yet beheld such a God, except you and alone; for to those who wait for you, that is, to those who have made the hope in you, he lavishes the mercy; for it will wholly follow the workers of righteousness, and it will fit those to receive it who would be in memory of your ways, that is, accomplishers of your wills; for we say the ways of the Lord are his commandments. And indeed the divine David sings, at one time that, In your way I will live, at another again: The way of your commandments I ran, when you broadened my heart. Tome 6. [Lemma, Isaiah 64:5-7:] Behold you were angered, and we sinned. Because of this we strayed, and we all became like unclean, and all our righteousness like a rag of a woman sitting apart; and we fell off like leaves because of our lawlessnesses; thus wind will carry us like dust, and there is not the one calling on your name, and the one remembering to take hold of you, because you turned your face away from us, and handed us over because of our sins. It seemed good to some of the interpreters to approach the things set before us according to another sense. For they reverse the rendering of the words, or the force of the thoughts, so that the thing said may be such: Behold we sinned, and you were angered. For not indeed, they say, did the divine anger become a cause for them of offending. But since they themselves acted outrageously, God was angered; for they fear, as is likely, lest somehow the divine wrath be understood a procurer of sin. But I think it needful to say that: for it has no accusation against the divine anger, that those who have come under it are unable toward being able to escape the attack of sin. For as long as the one saving delights in us, we prevail over sin, and departing strongly from the filths from baseness we are crowned with the glories toward spiritual manliness. But embittering the supplier of the strength, and the president of the manliness, we fall into the strengthless, and helpless[ness] [the section breaks off mid-word].
pass_b_english: … shows his gentleness, unexpectedly saving those who have slipped away from every hope, and holding out a saving hand to those who are down low and lying, as it were, on the ground. Those who offer up the prayer before us say something like this: “From the foundation of the world we have neither heard of nor seen any such God, except you, and you alone” (compare Isaiah 64:4).

For to those who wait for you, that is, to those who have set their hope on you, he lavishes his mercy. For it will surely follow those who work righteousness, and it will be fitting for those to receive it who keep your ways in memory, that is, who carry out your will (compare Isaiah 64:4–5). For we say that the ways of the Lord are his commandments. So the inspired David sings at one time, “In your way I shall live” (compare Psalm 119:37), and at another, “I ran the way of your commandments, when you enlarged my heart” (Psalm 119:32).

Tomos 6. “See, you were angry, and we sinned. Therefore we went astray, and we all became like the unclean, and all our righteousness like the rag of a woman in her impurity. We fell away like leaves because of our lawless deeds; so the wind will carry us off like dust. There is no one who calls on your name, or who remembers to take hold of you; for you turned your face away from us and handed us over because of our sins” (Isaiah 64:5–7).

Some of the interpreters decided to approach these words with a different sense. They reverse the order of the words, or rather the force of the thoughts, so that the saying becomes: “See, we sinned, and you were angry.” For the divine anger, they say, did not become the cause of their offending; rather, because they had behaved outrageously, God was angry. They fear, naturally enough, that the divine wrath might somehow be thought to bring about sin.

But I think this must be said: it is no charge against the divine wrath that those who have come under it are unable to escape the assault of sin. For as long as the One who saves us takes delight in us, we rise far above sin, and, keeping firmly away from the filth that comes from wickedness, we are crowned with the glories of spiritual courage. But when we embitter the Giver of our strength and the Lord of our courage, we fall into weakness and help…

choices.term:
διασώζων ἀδοκή- τως τοὺς ἐξ ἁπάσης ἐλπίδος ὠ
λισθηκότας
choices.english: unexpectedly saving those who have slipped away from every hope
choices.why: God saves those who had fallen from all hope; not 'unbelievers are saved from their hopes'.
rejected: unbelievers are saved from their hopes

choices.english: Those who offer up the prayer before us
choices.why: The speakers of Isaiah 64:4-5, not 'those who bring forth the set stone'.
rejected: those who bring forth the set stone

choices.english: the rag of a woman in her impurity
choices.why: A woman set apart during her period (Septuagint Isaiah 64:6).

choices.term: Ἀναστρέφουσι γὰρ τῶν λέξεων τὴν ἀπόδοσιν
choices.english: They reverse the order of the words
choices.why: The reversal 'we sinned, and you were angry' belongs to other interpreters; Cyril answers it.
The word breaks off mid-word (ἀδραν…, 'helplessness'); nothing is supplied.
